title: August 2026 Visa Bulletin Delivers Big Family Green Card Gains but Freezes Employment Path for Indians
excerpt: The F-2A category for spouses of permanent residents jumped 18 months to near-current status, while EB-2 and EB-5 India remain unavailable until the new fiscal year begins in October.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • F-2A family category advanced 18 months, now effectively current for most applicants.
  • F-1 category for unmarried adult children jumped over 10 months to December 15, 2018.
  • EB-2 and EB-5 categories for India remain unavailable until fiscal year 2027 starts.
  • EB-1 India is frozen at October 15, 2022, with potential for further retrogression.
  • Family-based applicants should act quickly to avoid missing opportunities as dates may retrogress.

August 2026 Visa Bulletin
  • The F-2A family category advanced over 18 months to July 22, 2026 — effectively current — benefiting spouses and minor children of green card holders across all countries.
  • F-1 dates for unmarried adult children of US citizens leaped more than 10 months forward to December 15, 2018, while F-4 sibling petitions gained 8 months.
  • EB-2 and EB-5 Unreserved for India remain marked "Unavailable" through September 30, with no new visa numbers until fiscal year 2027 begins on October 1.
  • EB-1 India is frozen at October 15, 2022, and EB-3 India is stuck at January 1, 2014, with the State Department warning of possible further retrogression.

Family Categories See Sweeping Advances

The U.S. State Department released the August 2026 Visa Bulletin this week, delivering a mixed verdict for the millions of applicants waiting in green card queues. Family-sponsored categories recorded their largest collective advance in months, while employment-based pathways for Indian-born applicants remained frozen or unavailable for the third consecutive bulletin.

https://x.com/Newsweek/status/2079476229942419911 > **"State Department released the August 2026 Visa Bulletin this week, delivering a mixed verdict for the millions of applicants waiting in green card queues."**

The most dramatic movement came in the F-2A category, which covers spouses and minor unmarried children of lawful permanent residents. The Final Action Date jumped from January 1, 2025 to July 22, 2026 — a leap of roughly 18 months — making the category effectively current for applicants from all countries except Mexico, which advanced to July 22, 2025. For Indian families with pending F-2A petitions, this means eligible applicants can now move forward with interview scheduling or adjustment of status filings.

"State Department released the August 2026 Visa Bulletin this week, delivering a mixed verdict for the millions of applicants waiting in green card queues."

The F-1 category for unmarried adult sons and daughters of U.S. citizens also saw a strong push forward. Priority dates advanced more than 10 months to December 15, 2018 for most countries, according to the bulletin. The F-4 category for siblings of U.S. citizens gained eight months for the "All Other Countries" and China chargeability areas, moving to September 1, 2009, though India's F-4 date remained stuck at November 1, 2006.

Employment-Based India: A Grim Picture Persists

For Indian-born professionals relying on employment-based green card pathways, the August bulletin offers no relief. The EB-2 category — the most widely used route for skilled workers in technology, healthcare and engineering — remains marked "Unavailable," a status that has been in effect since May 2026 when the State Department announced that all EB-2 visa numbers for India had been exhausted for fiscal year 2026.

"Your category is unavailable through September 30, 2026. You cannot file I-485 or receive a consular immigrant visa in August or September regardless of how long your I-140 has been approved."

— Hasan Legal PC, immigration law analysis

EB-5 Unreserved for India is similarly unavailable, blocking investor-visa applicants from final processing. EB-1, covering priority workers including those with extraordinary ability and multinational executives, remains frozen at October 15, 2022, after a two-month retrogression earlier this year. EB-3 India, which serves professionals and skilled workers, is unchanged at January 1, 2014 — a date that reflects a backlog stretching over 12 years.

The EB-3 "All Other Countries" category did see a modest one-month advance to September 1, 2024, and EB-1 China moved forward one month to July 1, 2023. But the structural bottleneck for India remains the 7% per-country cap under the Immigration and Nationality Act, which limits India to approximately 9,800 employment-based green cards annually across all EB categories combined.

What to Expect Next

The State Department has flagged the risk of further retrogression or even an "Unavailable" designation for EB-1 India in the coming months if demand stays high. EB-2 China and EB-3 Philippines are also on watch lists for potential pullbacks before the fiscal year ends on September 30.

Immigration attorneys are advising EB-2 India applicants to use the current pause to prepare their I-485 filing packages — gathering civil documents, completing Form I-693 medical exams and updating financial evidence — so they can file immediately when the October 2026 bulletin reopens their category. The State Department has indicated that EB-2 India should reopen at or above July 15, 2014 when fiscal year 2027 begins.

For family-based applicants, the picture is brighter but carries its own warning. Immigration analysts note that the broad advances in F-1, F-2A and F-4 may slow in August and September as the State Department manages year-end visa number allocations to stay within annual limits. Applicants with newly current priority dates should move quickly to submit documentation and avoid missing the window if dates retrogress in the new fiscal year.

The August 2026 bulletin takes effect for visa issuances and adjustment of status filings beginning August 1.
nri_angle: Indian-born professionals face continued EB-2 and EB-5 unavailability through September, while Indian families benefit from the F-2A surge to near-current status.
